q-130094.name: Question 1
q-130094.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}-x+y,$ find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(1,-1).$
q-130094.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-x+y)\,j \\  & =({y}^{2}-1)\text{ }i+(2xy+1)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(1,-1) & =((-1)^{2}-1)\,i+(2(1)(-1)+1)\,j \\  & =0\,i-j \\  & =⟨0,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

q-36394.problem: Given the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(3,2).$
q-36394.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent line to the level curve $f(x,y)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(3,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y) & ={f}_{x}(x,y)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+5xy-5x{y}^{2})j \\  & =(2xy+5y-5{y}^{2})i+({x}^{2}+5x-10xy)j \\ ∇\,f(3,2) & =(2(3)(2)+5(2)-5(2)^{2})i+((3)^{2}+5(3)-10(3)(2))j \\  & =2\,i-36\,j \\  & =⟨2,-36⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the Cartesian equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0})$ can be written as:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(3,2)\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-36⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,\,y-2⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Given the function f(x,y)=x2y+5xy−5xy2, find the equation of the tangent line to the level curve that passes through the point where (x,y)=(3,2).

The equation of the tangent line to the level curve f(x,y)=k at the point (x0,y0) can be expressed as

∇f(x0,y0)⋅⟨x−x0,y−y0⟩=0.

q-130200.name: Question 3
q-130200.problem: Consider the plane curve $x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}=e-y.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(1,0).$
q-130200.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1} & =e-y \\ x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y & =e\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=e.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(1,0)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(1,0)={f}_{y}(1,0)i-{f}_{x}(1,0)j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(1,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+y)j \\  & =(2xy{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}+1)i-{e}^{{y}^{2}+1}\,j \\ t(1,0) & =(2(1)(0){e}^{0+1}+1)i-{e}^{0+1}\,j \\  & =i-e\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $i-e\,j.$

q-36391.name: Question 4
q-36391.problem: Consider the plane curve ${x}^{2}y=xy+4.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(2,2).$
q-36391.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y & =xy+4 \\ {x}^{2}y-xy & =4\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y-xy$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=4.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(2,2)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(2,2)={f}_{y}(2,2)\,i-{f}_{x}(2,2)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-xy)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-xy)\,j \\  & =({x}^{2}-x)\,i-(2xy-y)\,j \\ t(2,2) & =({2}^{2}-2)\,i-(2(2)(2)-2)\,j \\  & =2\,i-6\,j\end{aligned}
$$

q-130221.name: Question 5
q-130221.problem: At which points on the curve $2xy=2x-y$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $2\,i-j?$
q-130221.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy & =2x-y \\ 2xy-2x+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy-2x+y,$ our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-2x+y)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-2x+y)\,j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i-(2y-2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $2\,i-j,$ we must have $t\cdot (2\,i-j)=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot (2\,i-j) & =0 \\ ((2x+1)\,i-(2y-2)\,j)\cdot (2\,i-j) & =0 \\ (4x+2)+(2y-2) & =0 \\ 4x+2y & =0 \\ y & =-2x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=-2x$ into the equation of our curve gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy & =2x-y \\ 2x(-2x) & =2x-(-2x) \\ -4{x}^{2} & =4x \\ 4{x}^{2}+4x & =0 \\ 4x(x+1) & =0 \\ x & =-1\,\text{or}\,x=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

- For $x=-1,$ we get $y=2,$ and the corresponding point is $(-1,2).$

- For $x=0,$ we get $y=0,$ and the corresponding point is $(0,0).$

q-72416.name: Question 6
q-72416.problem: At which points on the curve $2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y$ is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector $j?$
q-72416.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}=-y \\ 2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2xy-3{x}^{2}+y$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows:

$$
t(x,y)={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & ={f}_{y}(x,y)\,i-{f}_{x}(x,y)\,j \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy-3{x}^{2}+y)j \\  & =(2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to $j$, we must have $t\cdot j=0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y)\cdot j & =0 \\ ((2x+1)\,i-2(y-3x)\,j)\cdot j & =0 \\ -2(y-3x) & =0 \\ y & =3x\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $y=3x$ into the equation of our curve gives:  

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy-3{x}^{2}+y & =0 \\ 2x(3x)-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 6{x}^{2}-3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2}+3x & =0 \\ 3x(x+1) & =0 \\ x & =0\,\text{or}\,x=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally:

Question 6
?

At which points on the curve 2xy−3x2=−y is the tangent vector to the curve perpendicular to the vector j?

a
(0,−1) and (0,−3)
b
(0,3) and (0,−3)
c
(0,0) and (−1,−3)
d
(3,0) and (−1,0)
e
(0,1) and (1,−3)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we bring all variables to one side: 2xy−3x2=−y2xy−3x2+y=0

If we set f(x,y)=2xy−3x2+y, our curve can be viewed as the level curve f(x,y)=0.

A tangent vector to the level curve can be computed as follows: t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j

So, we calculate t(x,y):

t(x,y)=fy(x,y)i−fx(x,y)j=∂∂y(2xy−3x2+y)i−∂∂x(2xy−3x2+y)j=(2x+1)i−2(y−3x)j

Since our tangent vector needs to be perpendicular to j, we must have t⋅j=0.

t(x,y)⋅j=0((2x+1)i−2(y−3x)j)⋅j=0−2(y−3x)=0y=3x

Substituting y=3x into the equation of our curve gives:

2xy−3x2+y=02x(3x)−3x2+3x=06x2−3x2+3x=03x2+3x=03x(x+1)=0x=0orx=−1

Finally:

  • If x=0, we get y=0 and the corresponding point is (0,0).

  • If x=−1, we get y=−3 and the corresponding point is (−1,−3).
